text.p: Italian bonds, futures and currency took a late hammering after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer reiterated his view that one-off measures would not be enough to qualify for EMU, which he expected to start on time in 1999.

Spanish bonos fell on similar, tacit fears that both countries might not make the grade to join a single currency in time. Italian Btp futures slumped more than 150 basis points but recovered to trade off 143 points at 121.71 by 1551 GMT.
"It seems to have been triggered by Tietmeyer this morning although his comments weren't that negative," said one trader. "Such a large move on no news is disturbing for Btps."
The mood sent the lira sharply lower against the mark.
But the trader added: "No-one commented when the market went up 10 points, so it's a correction...It's just a blip, but if we see another day like this, we might see a bigger sell-off."

Another dealer added: "The market hasn't wanted to listen to the tough talking coming from Germany and for several days it's carried on living EMU optimism. Today, though, it woke up, probably also because we'd got to pretty unattractive yields."
Dealers said U.S. institutions unwinding excessively long positions triggered the fall. One saw next support around 121.
Tietmeyer welcomed Italy's EMU efforts and said it would be welcome if it fulfilled the criteria "in a lasting way".
